ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$. Point $I$ is the intersection point of the angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle AIC = 124^\circ$. Point $E$ is on the extension line of side $AD$. What is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that point I is the intersection of the angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAC = 2\angle IAC$, $\angle ACB = 2\angle ICA$, \\
Given $\angle AIC = 124^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle IAC + \angle ICA = 180^\circ - \angle AIC = 56^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle B = 180^\circ - (\angle BAC + \angle ACB) = 180^\circ - 2(\angle IAC + \angle ICA) = 180^\circ - 2 \times 56^\circ = 68^\circ$, \\
Furthermore, since quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O, \\
$\therefore \angle CDE = \angle B = \boxed{68^\circ}$.
